A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from MuSL to QiMeng-MuPa. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–H are accessible and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original code-translation and unit-test-generation experiments, ablations, error analyses and CUDA speedup measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds training-round coverage measurements and speedup comparisons across rounds and input sizes.

M1.justification: The Translator–Tester architecture, Co-verify filtering, Co-evolve back-translation and training objectives remain unchanged. QiMeng-MuPa is a renaming; Claude-assisted input construction serves an added evaluation, and reinforcement learning is only future work.

E1.justification: BabelTower and the C/CUDA tasks remain unchanged. V2 extends the reported speedup input scenarios with rectangular matrices and sizes reaching 16,384 × 16,384 in Figure 10, beyond the sizes up to 8,192 reported for three selected kernels in v1 Table 5.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark, ablation, error-analysis and case-study comparisons retain their comparator sets, including TransCoder, CodeRosetta and the GPT and DeepSeek models. Claude 4-Sonnet constructs evaluation-input templates in v2; it is not an evaluated competing translator.

E3.justification: V2 adds per-round coverage evaluation using translated C as a proxy for CUDA, plus Claude-designed templates and randomized inputs for speedup testing. Appendix D.2 revises the stated chat-template choice from Llama3 alone to Llama3 or Qwen2.5; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.2 tests whether generated-test coverage deteriorates during iterative training. Appendix C.3 adds speedup comparisons across training rounds and input sizes, supplementing the retained three-kernel examples. Existing filtering/freezing ablations, error analyses and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new coverage and speedup plots add point results without introducing uncertainty estimation; the existing descriptive statistics and correlation analysis are retained.

E6.justification: V2 adds concrete coverage and speedup curves in Figures 5 and 10. Existing benchmark results remain unchanged: Qwen2.5-Coder with the framework still achieves 85.15% Pass@1 in Table 1, and Table 5 retains its original speedup entries.

T1.justification: The functional-equivalence definitions, verified-triplet construction, cross-entropy objectives and metric formulas retain the same mathematics. No assumptions, proofs or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: V2 adds an introduction claim that this is the first domain-specific LLM capable of automatic code parallelization for HPC. The central mutual-supervision contribution, dataset contribution and headline performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of maintained test quality and improved runtime robustness/scalability. Appendix H explicitly identifies limited training diversity, sharpens the existing test-set limitation around simple correctness-focused cases, and replaces broader-language/corpus-expansion plans with reinforcement learning for kernel efficiency.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 removes the explicit i-epochs-per-iteration schedule and PyTorch DDP training on eight A100-80GB GPUs. V2 adds input-construction and CUDA-coverage-proxy details for its new analyses and updates the stated repository address from musl to mupa.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion remain unchanged. The added first-domain-specific-LLM claim in the introduction strengthens the work's novelty positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: V2 updates the title and method terminology, adds acknowledgements, inserts Appendix A.2 and revises the speedup and limitations passages. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 5 and 10, redraws Figure 4 with revised axes and legends, and corrects its panel descriptions. Tables are reformatted, including removal of Table 1's open-source column. Most existing figures and code displays are retained with renumbering or relocation.

improvement.justification: The added coverage and scaling analyses provide useful evidence, and Appendix H states limitations more explicitly. However, v2 removes the training epoch schedule and hardware details, while its new no-degradation interpretation is only partly supported: Figure 5 shows C branch-taking coverage falling from about 95% to 89%. These benefits and losses in reproducibility and interpretive precision leave the net quality direction uncertain.
